message.content: **Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28) and checked the live quote ($222.70 last, $222.72 ask), then bought **44 shares of AAPL at a $222.72 limit (filled at $222.72, ≈$9,799.68)** — within the $10,000/order and $20,000/day caps and with no fund transfers. My decision was based on a strong, cash-generative business: net sales of **$391,035M** (+2%), gross margin expanding to **46.2%**, Services up 13% to $96,169M at a 73.9% margin, operating income of **$123,216M** (+7.8%), and operating cash flow of **$118,254M**, backed by ~$140.8B of unrestricted cash/securities and a $110B buyback plus dividend. Net income of **$93,736M** (diluted EPS **$6.08**) dipped only because of a one-time $10.2B State Aid tax charge — pre-tax income actually rose to $123,485M — so the reported headline of $113,736M net income / $7.38 EPS in the filing's "restatement" note and income-statement face is internally inconsistent (it doesn't reconcile with the tax provision, segment totals, cash-flow statement, or the EPS note) and I did not rely on it. At ~36x trailing EPS the valuation is full but reasonable for Apple's quality and cash generation, so I initiated a modest starter position; the account now holds $50,000 cash minus the fill, 100 MSFT shares, and 44 AAPL shares.
